author: Thayer & Bangs, 1909

art.subject: Zappey's Flycatcher (Cyanoptila cumatilis), adult male, as seen on Korean islands during spring migration: crown bright turquoise-blue; upperparts, wings and tail deep blue with a slight turquoise tone; face, chin, throat and upper breast deep blue, a little darker and duller than the crown but never black, continuous with the blue of the head; lower breast and belly clean white, sharply divided from the blue; white bases to the outer tail feathers. Bill black; dark eye; legs black.
art.pose: perched upright on a branch in the forest mid-storey, side view
art.scene: mixed broadleaf forest on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in May; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Fairly large flycatcher, larger than a sparrow, the same size and shape as Blue-and-white Flycatcher. Upright posture; round head with no crest, the crown feathers lie flat. Bill black, broad-based and flat, shorter than the head. Legs short, black. Long wings with a long primary projection. Tail medium length, square-ended. Sits still on mid-level branches and sallies out for insects.
avoid: Do not paint a black face, throat and breast; that is Blue-and-white Flycatcher (Cyanoptila cyanomelana).
Do not extend the blue onto the belly; the belly is clean white.
Do not add wing-bars or a white supercilium.
